INTEGRATED SCIENCE — TERMLY EXAM #18
====

GRADE: Grade 9
SUBJECT: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. pascal (Pa)
   B. watt (W)
   C. joule (J)
   D. newton (N)

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Metals and Alloys? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Metals and Alloys.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Metals and Alloys.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Metals and Alloys.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Metals and Alloys.

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Nutrition in animals? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Nutrition in animals.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Nutrition in animals.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Nutrition in animals.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Nutrition in animals.

4. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   B. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   C. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   D. A mixture always has a fixed melting point

5. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Decomposers only
   B. Producers
   C. Primary consumers only
   D. Tertiary consumers

6. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. A chemical reaction forming ash
   B. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   C. Heating until a solid melts
   D. Movement of water only across a membrane

7. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any substance that conducts electricity
   B. Any white crystal used in cooking
   C. A mixture of two liquids
   D. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

8. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Ice melting to water
   B. Paper burning to ash
   C. Iron rusting
   D. Milk souring

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Structure of the atom? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Structure of the atom.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Structure of the atom.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Structure of the atom.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Structure of the atom.

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The Interdependence of Life? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The Interdependence of Life.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Interdependence of Life.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to The Interdependence of Life.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on The Interdependence of Life.

11. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Removing all vegetation
   B. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   C. Burning crop residue every week
   D. Overgrazing continuously

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Reproduction in plants? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Reproduction in plants.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Reproduction in plants.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Reproduction in plants.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Reproduction in plants.

13. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Glucose and oxygen
   B. Only water vapour
   C. Only carbon dioxide
   D. Nitrogen gas only

14. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Curved mirrors? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Curved mirrors.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Curved mirrors.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Curved mirrors.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Curved mirrors.

15. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Water hardness? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Water hardness.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water hardness.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Water hardness.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Water hardness.

16. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 100 °C
   B. 37 °C
   C. 0 °C
   D. 50 °C

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
17. In three clear sentences, explain Metals and Alloys and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Water hardness and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Nutrition in animals and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Reproduction in plants and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain The Interdependence of Life and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Curved mirrors and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

2. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Metals and Alloys.

4. B — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

5. B — Producers

8. A — Ice melting to water

10. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Interdependence of Life.
